title: Dedicated GPU carving, adaptive backpressure, and noisy-neighbor containment
creator: Priya Patel
description: Design and implement a tenant-facing GPU "carving" model that guarantees throughput SLOs while enabling adaptive autoscaling and fast noisy-neighbor containment without full hard-slicing of hardware. Focus is on predictable p50/p95 latency and long-window throughput contracts for Dedicated customers.
goals: Provide per-tenant throughput contracts (tokens/sec and sustained throughput) that are enforceable without preemptive VM-level reboots
Implement an adaptive backpressure admission controller that uses short-window latency signals to shift requests to fallback model variants or lower-cost lanes
Detect noisy-neighbor patterns in real time using double-pass attribution and sequence-length-aware signals and apply graduated containment (soft throttle, cache isolation, selective eviction)
Expose tenant-visible quota metrics and incident playbooks for operators and SREs
non_goals: Full MIG-based hard-slicing across all GPU families (may be future work)
Replacing Dedicated hard reservations — this augments, not supplants, existing reservation contracts
Deep model-level quality mitigation (model retraining) — only routing/serving mitigations are in scope
acceptance_criteria: New admission controller enforces token-bucket quota per-tenant and maintains >=95% success for SLO-bound tenants under 70% fleet utilization in synthetic tests
Noisy-neighbor detector triggers containment actions within 45s median from spike start in staged chaos tests
Metrics for per-tenant throughput, p50/p95 latency, cache-hit ratio, and eviction-rate are visible in Grafana dashboards
Canary rollout to 5 dedicated pools with automated rollback on increased customer error-rate or >10% latency regression
design_decisions: Use a two-tier quota model: soft token-bucket with decay (preferred path) and hard emergency budget for critical tenants
Admission controller computes per-request cost using sequence-length estimate + model profile and deducts from tenant tokens
KV-cache isolation implemented via namespace tagging and LRU-based soft partitions (no global reconfiguration required)

Noisy-neighbor detection uses a double-pass: first detect anomalies in tenant-level throughput/latency, then attribute to kernel-level signals (CUDA SM util, memory-bandwidth, PCIe stalls) to avoid false positives
Autoscaler is predictive: 30s short-window spike detector + 5m trend predictor to decide immediate burst nodes vs scheduled scale-up
Fallback policy prefers lower-cost quantized model variants with structured output validation before returning to caller
tradeoffs: Soft partitioning preserves multiplexing efficiency but offers weaker isolation versus full MIG/hard-slice — chosen to optimize unit cost for typical workloads
Sequence-length-aware costing improves fairness for long-sequence jobs but requires accurate sequence prediction heuristics and increases admission-controller CPU usage
Cache namespace isolation reduces cross-tenant KV-cache pollution but can lower overall cache hit-rates (accepting some hit-rate loss for isolation guarantees)
implementation_plan: RFC: publish high-level design and cost model (PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rfcs/pull/412)
Prototype admission controller in Rust sidecar and load-test against existing Dedicated pools
Instrument model profiles: per-model per-sequence-cost table computed by benchmark harness
Implement noisy-neighbor detector service that ingests kernel-level telemetry and tenant metrics
Integrate containment actions into orchestrator: soft-throttle, cache-namespace split, selective KV-eviction
Add dashboards and alerting rules; add canary rollout automation and feature-flag gating
rollout_plan: Alpha: internal Dedicated pools only, 1 pool, monitor for 2 weeks
Beta: invite 3 low-risk customers with opt-in and real-time dashboard access
Canary: automated canary across 5 pools with rollback triggers (error-rate, latency, cost anomalies)
GA: enable on new Dedicated clusters and offer opt-in migration for existing customers
test_plan: Unit tests for admission controller cost calculation and bucket accounting
Synthetic workload tests: mixed long/short sequences, bursty traffic, and background noise
Chaos tests: introduce synthetic kernel contention (gpu-stress) and validate detection-to-containment latency
Stability test: 72h soak with sustained 80% utilization and periodic spikes
Customer-facing beta with detailed telemetry collection
updates: 2025-02-12: Ticket created. Initial scope drafted after tabletop with SRE and Product. Assigned to Marco Ruiz.
2025-02-20: Prototype admission-controller sidecar started (Rust). Benchmarked per-sequence cost estimator using benchmark harness. Risk: estimator adds ~3ms per request CPU overhead.
2025-02-28: Noisy-neighbor detector MVP ingests kernel-level telemetry via new metric stream. Built simple rule-based attribution; precision ~0.82 on synthetic traces.
2025-03-05: Decision to prefer soft partitioning and cache namespace tags to avoid expensive MIG conversions. Documented in RFC (link in links).
2025-03-10: Canary automation implemented; ready for alpha rollout once on-call playbook is finalized. Security review not required for initial alpha.
